questions.question: A parallel-plate capacitor has plate area $A = 0.02\ \mathrm{m^2}$, plate separation $d = 2\ \mathrm{mm}$, and vacuum between the plates. Find its capacitance. ($\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\ \mathrm{F/m}$)
A capacitor $C = 10\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ is connected to a battery of $V = 12\ \mathrm{V}$. Find: (a) the charge stored, (b) the energy stored.

Two capacitors $C_1 = 4\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ and $C_2 = 6\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ are connected in parallel to a $V = 10\ \mathrm{V}$ battery. Find: (a) the equivalent capacitance, (b) the total charge, (c) the energy stored in each.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Parallel: $C_{\text{eq}} = C_1 + C_2 = 4 + 6 = 10\ \mu\mathrm{F}$

**(b)** $Q = C_{\text{eq}} V = 10\times10^{-6} \times 10 = 100\ \mu\mathrm{C}$

(Same voltage across each: $Q_1 = 40\ \mu\mathrm{C}$, $Q_2 = 60\ \mu\mathrm{C}$)

**(c)** $U_1 = \frac{1}{2}C_1 V^2 = \frac{1}{2}(4\times10^{-6})(100) = 2\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{J}$

$U_2 = \frac{1}{2}C_2 V^2 = \frac{1}{2}(6\times10^{-6})(100) = 3\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{J}$

questions.question: Two capacitors $C_1 = 3\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ and $C_2 = 6\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ are connected in series to a $V = 9\ \mathrm{V}$ battery. Find: (a) the equivalent capacitance, (b) the total charge, (c) the voltage across each.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Series: $\dfrac{1}{C_{\text{eq}}} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$C_{\text{eq}} = 2\ \mu\mathrm{F}$

**(b)** $Q = C_{\text{eq}} V = 2\times10^{-6} \times 9 = 18\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ (same on both capacitors in series)

**(c)** $V_1 = Q/C_1 = 18/3 = 6\ \mathrm{V}$; $V_2 = Q/C_2 = 18/6 = 3\ \mathrm{V}$

Check: $V_1 + V_2 = 6 + 3 = 9\ \mathrm{V}$ ✓

questions.question: A parallel-plate capacitor has capacitance $C_0$ with vacuum. A dielectric with $\kappa = 3$ fills the space between the plates. Find: (a) the new capacitance, (b) if connected to a fixed battery of voltage $V$, how does the stored charge change?
questions.answer:
**(a)** $C = \kappa C_0 = 3C_0$

The dielectric reduces the electric field inside (polarization of the dielectric), allowing more charge to be stored at the same voltage.

**(b)** With fixed voltage $V$: $Q = CV = 3C_0 V = 3Q_0$

The stored charge **triples** when the dielectric is inserted (while connected to the battery).

The electric field inside: $E = V/d$ — unchanged (same $V$, same $d$).

questions.question: Three capacitors are arranged: $C_1 = 2\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ and $C_2 = 4\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ in series, and this combination in parallel with $C_3 = 5\ \mu\mathrm{F}$. The battery is $V = 12\ \mathrm{V}$. Find: (a) the total equivalent capacitance, (b) the charge on $C_3$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Series combination: $C_{12} = \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} = \dfrac{2 \times 4}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3}\ \mu\mathrm{F}$

Parallel with $C_3$: $C_{\text{eq}} = C_{12} + C_3 = \dfrac{4}{3} + 5 = \dfrac{19}{3} \approx 6.33\ \mu\mathrm{F}$

**(b)** $C_3$ has full battery voltage across it: $Q_3 = C_3 V = 5\times10^{-6} \times 12 = 60\ \mu\mathrm{C}$

questions.question: Show the three equivalent forms of the energy stored in a capacitor: $U = \frac{1}{2}CV^2 = \frac{Q^2}{2C} = \frac{1}{2}QV$.
questions.answer:
Starting from the definition: the work done to charge a capacitor from $0$ to charge $Q$:

$dW = V\,dq = \dfrac{q}{C}\,dq$

$U = \int_0^Q \dfrac{q}{C}\,dq = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C}$

Since $Q = CV$ and $V = Q/C$:

$\dfrac{Q^2}{2C} = \dfrac{(CV)^2}{2C} = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^2$ ✓

$\dfrac{Q^2}{2C} = \dfrac{Q \cdot (Q/C)}{2} = \dfrac{QV}{2}$ ✓

All three forms are equivalent and useful in different contexts.

questions.question: A capacitor $C = 20\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ is charged to $V_0 = 100\ \mathrm{V}$, then disconnected from the battery. The plate separation is then doubled. Find the new voltage and the change in stored energy.
questions.answer:
Disconnected: charge $Q = C_0 V_0 = 20\times10^{-6} \times 100 = 2\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{C}$ is constant.

Doubling $d$ halves $C$: $C' = C_0/2 = 10\ \mu\mathrm{F}$

New voltage: $V' = Q/C' = 2\times10^{-3}/(10\times10^{-6}) = 200\ \mathrm{V}$

Original energy: $U_0 = \frac{1}{2}C_0 V_0^2 = \frac{1}{2}(20\times10^{-6})(10^4) = 0.1\ \mathrm{J}$

New energy: $U' = \frac{Q^2}{2C'} = \frac{(2\times10^{-3})^2}{2 \times 10\times10^{-6}} = \frac{4\times10^{-6}}{2\times10^{-5}} = 0.2\ \mathrm{J}$

$\Delta U = 0.2 - 0.1 = 0.1\ \mathrm{J}$ (energy increased — stored by the work done pulling the plates apart)

questions.question: A $C_1 = 4\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor charged to $V_1 = 12\ \mathrm{V}$ is connected in parallel with an uncharged $C_2 = 8\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor. Find the final voltage across both.
questions.answer:
Charge is conserved (charges redistribute):

$Q_{\text{total}} = C_1 V_1 + 0 = 4\times10^{-6} \times 12 = 48\ \mu\mathrm{C}$

Final: both capacitors at the same voltage $V_f$:

$Q_{\text{total}} = (C_1 + C_2)V_f$

$V_f = \dfrac{Q_{\text{total}}}{C_1 + C_2} = \dfrac{48\times10^{-6}}{12\times10^{-6}} = 4\ \mathrm{V}$

Energy before: $\frac{1}{2}C_1 V_1^2 = \frac{1}{2}(4\times10^{-6})(144) = 288\ \mu\mathrm{J}$

Energy after: $\frac{1}{2}(C_1+C_2)V_f^2 = \frac{1}{2}(12\times10^{-6})(16) = 96\ \mu\mathrm{J}$

Energy lost to heat/radiation: $288 - 96 = 192\ \mu\mathrm{J}$

questions.question: The capacitance per unit area of a parallel-plate capacitor is $C/A = \varepsilon_0/d$. (a) A capacitor has $C = 1\ \mathrm{pF}$ and $d = 1\ \mathrm{mm}$. Find $A$. (b) Compare this to a $1\ \mathrm{cm} \times 1\ \mathrm{cm}$ square and comment on realistic capacitors.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $C/A = \varepsilon_0/d \Rightarrow A = Cd/\varepsilon_0$

$A = \dfrac{1\times10^{-12} \times 1\times10^{-3}}{8.85\times10^{-12}} = \dfrac{10^{-15}}{8.85\times10^{-12}} \approx 1.13\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2}$

$= 113\ \mathrm{cm^2}$

**(b)** $1\ \mathrm{cm} \times 1\ \mathrm{cm} = 1\ \mathrm{cm^2} = 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2}$ — so $1\ \mathrm{pF}$ requires about $113\ \mathrm{cm^2}$ of plate area.

Real capacitors use: (1) very small separation $d$, (2) dielectrics ($\kappa > 1$), and (3) rolled/stacked plates to achieve large $C$ in small volume.
